history.value: Founded in 2005 in Boston by Todd Dagres, Santo Politi, Paul Conway and Bijan Sabet with a $265M first fund, Spark Capital became one of the defining consumer-internet investors of the 2000s and 2010s: the Series A or B backer of Twitter (2008), Tumblr, Foursquare, Warby Parker, Wayfair, Oculus (sold to Facebook for $2B in 2014), Slack, Plaid (seed, 2013) and Cruise (Series A, 2015), with a Start@Spark seed program (2009) that funded first checks out of the main fund. A growth practice launched in 2014 (Spark Capital Growth Fund, $374M) added late positions in Affirm, Coinbase, Discord, Marqeta, Snap and Kalshi, and the firm led Anthropic's $450M Series C in 2023. One partnership runs both practices from San Francisco, New York and Boston. Nine early-stage funds (Spark Capital IX closed at $1.0B in 2026) and six growth funds (Growth Fund VI closed at $2.33B in 2026) sit under one exempt reporting adviser (CRD 161231) whose private funds held $15.6B of gross assets at the 2025 fiscal year end.
history.basis: Wikipedia (founders, fund sizes 2005-2024, Oculus sale, Anthropic Series C); the firm's Medium posts on the 2022 and 2024 funds; Form D filings for III, IV, Growth I-III, VI, IX and Growth VI (sources/edgar/fund-formds.json); ADV Section 7.B for the $15.6B gross asset value; entry stages from this run's base (Twitter Series A 2008, Plaid seed 2013, Cruise Series A 2015, Anthropic Growth 2023)

investment_concept.value: Spark Capital backs founders from the first check through growth, investing in consumer, enterprise software, fintech, crypto, hardware and AI companies with early-stage and growth funds run by one partnership.
investment_concept.basis: paraphrase of the site's belief statements ('Products can make markets', 'the decade-long journey', Early and Growth teams) and the sector list on Wikipedia ('consumer internet, enterprise software, gaming, infrastructure, hardware, semiconductors, crypto, fintech, and AI')

investment_stage.basis: entry-stage distribution of the 321 members: Seed 65, Series A 147, Growth 113 (Growth includes late positions such as Anthropic, Coinbase, Discord, Kalshi via the Growth funds)

investment_geo.basis: hq_country of the members: US ~88%; Europe (GB, DE, ES, NL, NO, RS, TR), Israel (Cyera, Fireblocks, Rapyd, Capitolis origin), Latin America (Nomad, Kavak-era rows) form the rest

investment_range.basis: Form D round sizes on member companies (313 non-pooled rounds): 10th percentile ≈ $1,130,000, median ≈ $10,339,997; upper limit = Baseten's $1.1B Series F (June 2026, Form D $1,096,448,855 sold), the largest round on a member's filings that Spark joined; round sizes are the round, not Spark's check
